site.name: fleetatlas
site.summary: FleetAtlas Fictional commercial fleet real-time management SaaS dashboard, used as a UXBench fixture. Pages - `index.html` — Fleet overview map home. Left thin rail nav; top bar with org switcher, view tabs (Map / List / Analytics), search box, alert bell (dropdown shows the 5 most recent on click); status filter strip (All / Running / Idle / Maintenance / Offline / Alert); full-screen SVG city map with 25 vehicles in real-time positions (running vehicles jitter their position every 5 seconds to simulate live updates); clicking a vehicle icon or drawer row → right detail panel slides in; bottom pull-up drawer showing the vehicle list. - Right detail panel (controlled by JS within the map page) — basic info (plate / model / year / VIN / fleet), driver info (with phone / shift / accumulated drive hours), current task (route / location / ETA / remaining miles), historical track SVG (24h / 7d / 30d toggle), fuel and speed sparklines; 4 action buttons (Send command / Contact driver / Maintenance record / Reassign task), with Reassign being a destructive action that has a second-confirmation modal. - `alerts.html` — Alerts center. 4 KPI cards (open / new today / by severity / mean handli

run_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore the core fleet management dashboard flow and verify the main adjacent pages, with emphasis on map/list switching, vehicle/alert drill-downs, and destructive action handling.
run_plan.summary: Start on the dashboard because it is the primary entry point and contains the richest interactive surface: org switching, view tabs, status filters, search, notification dropdown, map vehicle selection, and the bottom vehicle drawer. Then cover the standalone pages (Vehicles, Alerts, Analytics) to validate cross-page consistency, filtering/search behavior, and table/detail workflows. Finish with deeper validation of high-risk states such as alert handling, vehicle detail actions, and mobile viewport usability where small tap targets and unlabeled controls are most likely to regress.
assumptions: The visible dashboard controls are the primary route to vehicle detail and action workflows; side-nav placeholder items like Drivers, Routes, Maintenance, and Settings may not navigate to full pages and should only be probed cautiously.
The explorer should treat the prescan as authoritative: only index.html, vehicles.html, alerts.html, and analytics.html are known HTML pages.
The right-side vehicle detail panel and confirmation modal are implemented within index.html and should be validated through map/list interactions rather than expecting separate pages.
The alert bell dropdown on the dashboard contains the five most recent alerts, and the reassignment flow is the only explicitly noted destructive action.
risk_hotspots: index.html: org selector with missing label, search box, and Map/List/Analytics view toggles with small tap targets on mobile
index.html: alert bell dropdown and notification count state
index.html: vehicle click/drill-down into right detail panel, including 24h/7d/30d toggle and action buttons
index.html: Reassign task destructive action and second-confirmation modal
vehicles.html: dense filter/search/table controls and row-level details
alerts.html: multiple filters (time, severity, type, status) and Assign/Details actions on alert rows
analytics.html: report view integrity and any interaction on the lightweight controls present
mobile viewport: small tap targets and unlabeled select/input controls on all key pages

phases.title: Dashboard orientation and navigation
phases.objective: Validate the main landing experience and the top-level navigation controls before digging into deeper workflows.
key_checks: Confirm the default dashboard state loads with map view selected, status chips visible, and vehicle list drawer available
Exercise org switcher selection and verify the page updates consistently or remains stable
Check the notification bell dropdown contents and whether the count matches the visible alert badge
Try the top-level view toggles (Map view, List view, Analytics view) and note which ones change state versus navigate
Verify the status filter strip changes the visible vehicle set or highlights filtered state
exit_criteria: All visible top-bar controls on the dashboard have been clicked or at least state-checked once
Navigator behavior is understood for map/list/analytics tabs and alert dropdown
No blocking rendering or interaction issues are observed in the initial dashboard state

phases.title: Vehicle discovery and detail panel
phases.objective: Exercise the primary fleet workflow: finding a vehicle, opening details, and validating the vehicle-specific actions and history widgets.
key_checks: Use the search box with at least two query styles (plate and driver/route terms) to confirm filtering or matching behavior
Click representative vehicles from the map and from the drawer list, including at least one running vehicle and one non-running vehicle
Validate the right detail panel fields: basic info, driver info, current task, and historical track display
Switch the 24h/7d/30d history toggle and confirm the chart updates or the selected state changes
Check the four action buttons: Send command, Contact driver, Maintenance record, and Reassign task
Open Reassign task and verify the second-confirmation modal appears and is dismissible
Observe whether live map positions or status counts visibly change over time for running vehicles
exit_criteria: At least two distinct vehicle detail views have been opened successfully
The history toggle and all vehicle action buttons have been exercised or inspected
The destructive reassign confirmation path has been confirmed

phases.title: Vehicle list and filtering page
phases.objective: Validate the dedicated Vehicles page as the structured list/search/filter counterpart to the dashboard drawer.
key_checks: Open the Vehicles page and confirm the table/list is populated with vehicle rows and details actions
Test the status filter, fleet filter, and vehicle search field with representative inputs
Check whether selecting filters narrows the visible table rows and whether row counts remain sensible
Open at least one vehicle row detail action if available from the list
Confirm the page’s many inputs render and remain usable without overlap or truncation
exit_criteria: Search and both major filter types have been tried
At least one vehicle row has been inspected beyond the table summary
The page remains readable with dense data and no obvious layout collapse

phases.title: Alert triage workflow
phases.objective: Validate alert management, prioritization, and row-level actions on the Alerts page.
key_checks: Confirm KPI cards and the alert table are visible and coherent with the alert counts in navigation
Test the alert search field and the time, severity, type, and status filters individually
Exercise both Assign and Details actions on at least one high-severity alert row
Check that the filtered views still show plausible alert records and that row metadata updates accordingly
Look for any mismatch between alert severity/status filters and row contents
exit_criteria: All major filter categories have been interacted with
At least one alert row action has been triggered
The page behavior matches the expected alert triage pattern without broken controls

phases.title: Analytics verification
phases.objective: Confirm the analytical reporting page loads cleanly and the key dashboard metrics, heatmap, and ranking table are legible.
key_checks: Validate the headline KPIs and the fleet utilization heatmap render correctly
Inspect the driver performance ranking table for sorting/readability issues if sortable behavior exists
Exercise the visible search/control on this page and the org selector if it appears
Verify that the page remains stable on navigation from the dashboard analytics tab if that route is used
exit_criteria: The analytics page has been fully loaded and reviewed
Any visible control has been checked at least once
No data-visualization rendering issues are observed

phases.title: Mobile recheck of critical paths
phases.objective: Repeat the most important interactions in a mobile viewport to validate tap usability and responsive behavior.
key_checks: Recheck dashboard navigation, search, status chips, and notification/org controls on mobile
Verify that vehicle selection and detail opening still works without precision issues
Confirm the Vehicles and Alerts page filters remain operable and readable on smaller screens
Look for tap-target failures, clipped text, or hidden controls around the dense table/list layouts
exit_criteria: Critical dashboard, vehicle, and alert interactions have been attempted in mobile viewport
Any mobile-specific breakage is documented with page and control context
Coverage includes the controls already flagged as small tap targets in prescan

coverage_targets.pages: visit all known HTML pages and verify navigation between them from the dashboard entry point
coverage_targets.features: exercise most visible controls per key page, including search, filters, tabs, row actions, dropdowns, and the destructive reassign flow
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat critical checks on mobile viewport, prioritizing tap-target-sensitive controls and dense table/list layouts

notes: Treat the placeholder left-nav items that use '#' as low-priority unless they reveal real state changes; avoid spending excessive budget on dead-end links.
Prioritize at least one non-running vehicle and one critical alert because those are the most likely to expose edge-state bugs.
If the dashboard list drawer or map behavior is ambiguous, use the dedicated Vehicles page as the fallback source of truth for list interactions.
